message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news and bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (filled at $222.80, ~$8,912 total), which is within the mandate's $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps and leaves the $50,000 cash balance untouched otherwise (no money moved out; the only position was 100 MSFT). The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth-quarter report (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024), which showed quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year results of $391.0B in net sales, $93.7B in net income, $6.08 diluted EPS (including a one-time $10.2B tax charge), and $118.3B in operating cash flow — a resilient, cash-generative franchise. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as analysts weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, meaning I wasn't chasing a spike. The limit price was set just above the current quote ($222.70 last, $222.72 ask) to stay close to market while ensuring a fill.
